___ is a ___ with a history of hemorrhagic stroke

Per ___ records, Ms. ___ presented due to several days 
of worsening confusion at home, culminating in asking for her 
husband, who is dead.

She presented to her PCP's office, who 
obtained UA and CXR which were reportedly normal.

She was then 
admitted to the hospital, where she was found to be hypertensive 
to 241/86.

Her altered mental status was attributed to 
hypertensive encephalopathy.

However, it did not resolve when 
her blood pressure was controlled.

Neurology was consulted and recommended EEG and MRI for 
evaluation of her mental status.

However, the MRI could not be 
obtained due to the presence of her aneurysm clips.

An EEG was 
concerning for "sharp and slow wave discharges over the left 
temporal leads also focal slowing over the left hemispheric 
leads, no active evolution into seizure" per Dr. ___ 
discussion with the hospitalist at ___.

She was loaded 
with 1000 mg levetiracetam.

Given the possibility of infectious 
etiology, a lumbar puncture was obtained with 2 WBC (100% 
lymphs), 36 reds, Glucose 78 and protien 38.

She receieved 
acyclovir, doxycycline, vancomycin and ceftriaxone and a head CT 
and she was transferred to ___.

Could not assess review of systems due to patient's limited 
responsiveness.
Per medical records from ___,

1. History of hemorrhagic stroke secondary to aneurysm rupture 
in the left MCA territory, status post surgery and clips.

She 
now has expressive aphasia.
2. Colitis of unclear etiology, possibly Crohn's.

3. Memory loss written on the assisted living form, however, the 
family denies.

4. Kyphosis and possible collapse of T12 or L1 on chest x-ray 
from ___.
5. Hospitalization for dehydration in ___.

6. Peripheral venous stasis and lower extremity edema, however, 
not on any medication.
7. Abdominal aortic aneurysm.
8. Osteoporosis.

frequency in ___.
14. Status post total abdominal hysterectomy.
15. Vein stripping.

16. Shortness of breath thought to be due to kyphosis per 
daughter's report.
Per medical records from ___,
The patient has coronary artery disease in her family.

Her 
cousin had CHF.
Per our medical records,

Mother who died of Hodgkin's disease and first cousin with 
breast cancer.
Father had heart disease and emphysema.

___: IMPRESSION: This is an abnormal continuous video EEG 
monitoring study due to the presence of a slow, disorganized

___: IMPRESSION: This is an abnormal continuous video EEG

There is 
continuous delta slowing over the left parieto-occipital region, 
at times more diffusely over the left hemisphere.

These findings 
are consistent with a structural lesion causing focal cerebral 
dysfunction in the left posterior quadrant.

There are no 
definite epileptiform discharges or electrographic seizures.

Neurology Hospital Course

___ was transferred to the general neurology service 
in stable condition.
She remained persistently encephalopathic.
She remained hypertensive and was noted to have a leukocytosis.

Her EEG was negative for epileptogenic activity but did show a 
slow disorganized background consistent with encephalopathy.

Due 
to her history of aneurysm clips an MRI was postponed until 
definitive records could be obtained to verify safety.

In the 
meantime she underwent a thorough workup to rule out infectious 
etiologies, which was notable for: repeat LP with bland CSF; CT 
thorax which was negative for pneumonia or any evidence of 
abscess or malignancy; multiple urinalyses and urine cultures 
which were negative.

A toxic and metabolic workup was likewise 
negative.

Eventually an MRI was obtained which showed multiple 
strokes in the posterior circulation.

A thorough workup for the etiology of her strokes was notable 
for: telemetry showing normal sinus rhythm and echocardiogram 
with no evidence of thrombus, PFO or ASD; coagulation labs 
notable for an isolated elevation in DDimer which was attributed 
to her acute illness; CT thorax negative for evidence of 
malignancy, and lupus anticoagulant labs which are still 
pending.
Her HbA1c was normal and her lipids were not elevated.
She was started on a baby aspirin.

Her course was complicated by a diffuse maculopapular rash which 
arose in the context of newly started keppra and acyclovir.

These medications were discontinued as she had no electrographic 
evidence of seizure.

The acyclovir was subsequently restarted 
until her MRI was obtained.

She was hypertensive on admission and the amlodipine and 
labetalol she had been receiving at ___ were restarted 
with good effect.

She was noted to be dyspneic on exertion which 
was reportedly her baseline; she had no evidence of pneumonia or 
heart failure clinically or on imaging.

She became more alert and responsive but was noted to have 
worsened dysarthria, persistent disconjugate gaze, and failed 
swallow assessment on multiple occasions.

An NG tube was placed 
for enteral access.
A PEG tube was discussed with the family.
ICU COURSE
On ___ the pt was found to be hypotensive to 87/49.

She was 
afebrile with a T 98.7, HR 81, RR 11 and SO2 98% on RA.

A WBC 
count was elevated to 22.8 with 85% PMN.

Over those 24 hours, 
the pt became more somnolent with hypotension that was not fluid 
responsive.
A lactate was elevated to 3.5.

Previous blood 
cultures grew MSSA and enterobacter.

ID was consulted and they 
recommended Ceftriaxone monotherapy for MSSA and Enterobacter

(MSSA low grade can be treated with Ceftriaxone while high-grade 
would prefer Nafcillin).

Changed to Vanc/Zosyn when clinically 
deteriorated on ___ and she was covered empirically for Cdiff.
Her blood pressures and clinical status improved.

It was also 
noted, however, the the pt had a diffuse, blanchable pink 
erythamtous patch distributed across the chest, arms, and upper 
thighs while sparing the palms and soles.

There was no mucous 
membrane involvement, no desquamation.
The ddx was erythroderma
(likely 2'/2 pt's h/o psoriasis) vs drug rash.

Dermatology was 
not consulted, but the pt had relief of her pruritus with sarna.
Internal Medicine Hospital Course

On ___, having stabilized with fluids and broad spectrum 
antibiotics Ms. ___ was called out to the CC7 on the ___ A 
service.

# ___: Cr increased from 0.9 to 2.2 approximately 24 hours after 
receiving IV contrast in the setting of CT Abd/Pelvis and 
replacement of gastrostomy tube change.

Likely etiologies 
included contrast induced nephropathy and prerenal azotemia in 
the setting of infection.

FeNa <1% suggestive of pre-renal 
etiology, though contrast induced nephropathy can also present 
with a FeNa that looks pre-renal.

Her creatinine steadily 
improved to 1.1.

On ___, her creatinine increased to 1.4 in the 
setting of her new renal hematoma (see below) .

With 
transfusion, hydration and subsequent restarting of tube feeds, 
her creatinine returned to the normal range.
# Renal Hematoma: On ___, the patient's HCT dropped from 24 to
22 and her creatinine increased to 1.4.

The patient was taken 
to ___ to address bleeding around her G-tube.

A CT abdomen showed 
a subcapsular hematoma associated with her known right kidney 
mass.

She remained hemodynamically stable throughout this 
episode.

She responded appropriately to transfusion of 2 units 
of PRBCs.

Fondaparinux and aspirin were already being held for 
oozing around her G-tube.

Aspirin was restarted on ___, 
fondaparinux transiently restarted at therapeutic doses on ___lot, but replaced by heparin sc.

# Encephalopathy: Persistent toxic metabolic etiology vs 
multiple posterior circulation strokes as visualized on MRI on
TTE unremarkable.

Hypercoagulability workup notable for 
elevated DDimer, but ___ and fibrinogen WNL, lupus 
anticoagulant negative.

EEG was initially equivoval so she was 
started on Keppra, which was since discontinued given low 
suspicion for seizures.

Her LP was unremarkable with CSF 
additionally negative for both varicella and HSV.

Waxing and 
waning mental status and profound expressive asphasia persisted.
Per neurology, delirium may be side effect of occipital lesion.
Patient was maintained on delirium precautions.

Agitation was 
well-controlled with quetiapine.

She did require restraints 
until closer to the time of discharge.

# PEG tube: Patient has pulled at it several times due to 
encephalopathy, requiring replacement by ___ and subsequent 
causing bleeding from the immature tract.  ___ performed a 
contrast study and found it properly positioned with no hematoma 
and no active bleeding.

The oozing gradually resolved on its 
own.
Tube feeds were successfully resumed.

Restraints were used 
to attempt to prevent the patient from pulling the tube.
Over time, the pt began to take more food PO.

She continued to 
have pulling at the tube despite use of an abdominal binder and 
even after changing her tube feeds to bolus feeds.

At the end 
of her stay she completely pulled out the gastric tube.

After a 
discussion with her family (who did not want to use restraints) 
it was decided to leave out the gastric tube entirely.

The pt 
instead will have slow hand feeding and not have replacement of 
the feeding tube due to risk of harm and no clear benefit.

# Sepsis: The patient developed hypotension and increased 
lethargy ___ along with elevated WBC.
She was transferred to the
ICU, given IV fluids and antibiotics were broadened.

UA and CXR 
were unremarkable, C Diff was negative, blood cultures were 
negative.

Abdominal CT scan ruled out abscess or collection 
around G tube.

ID recommended a 14d bacteremia course at the 
time of her initial positive blood cultures.

She completed this 
course and antibiotics were discontinued.
#RUE clot: ___, PICC-associated.
PICC pulled on ___.

Continued 
prophylactic heparin sc, no need for further anticoagulation.

# Erythroderma: Likely drug induced eruption vs. psoriasis 
related erythroderma.
Improved without treatment.

Symptoms 
were controlled with sarna lotion.
Did try steroid cream.
# HIT: Antibody initially positive and heparin was discontinued.
SRA has since come back negative, making HIT very unlikely.
Thrombocytopenia has resolved.

She was restarted on sc heparin 
on ___

These were held during her ICU course and restarted for 
mild hypertension on the floor.
# Crohns disease: There was no evidence of active disease.

She 
was unable to take her home mesalamine 800 PO TID based on 
speech and swallow evaluation.
She was started on mesalamine
1000mg PR BID until cleared to take her home regimen by SLP.
